chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a female slave who is divorced, what is her waiting period? He said: Two menstrual cycles or two months. I said: And if her husband dies for her? He said: Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) said regarding the mothers of children: They do not marry until they complete a waiting period of four months and ten days, even if they are slaves.

key_terms.أُمَّهَاتُ الْأَوْلَادِ: Mothers of children (concubines who bore their master's child)
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: Waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a female slave slave upon divorce or death of her master according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the iddah of an umm al-walad, distinguishing between the shorter period of two menstruations for divorce and the longer four-month-and-ten-day period for the master's death. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that while the death iddah aligns with free women, the divorce iddah for slaves is distinct, reflecting the specific legal status of concubines in early Islamic jurisprudence.
